svg.aria-label: FareSight architecture in three layers: a capture pipeline that stores companion-app photos in TigerData Postgres and turns them into compressed Gaussian splats on a team Mac; a TigerData database authority behind Vercel serverless functions with OpenStreetMap and the MBTA V3 API as external sources; and a PlayCanvas WebXR runtime rendering on a Meta Quest 3 and in 2D on phones and laptops.
svg.text: 3 runtime layers • 11 Postgres tables on TigerData • 4 scene states • application-level capture pipeline

Storage: the companion app’s photos live in TigerData as bytea rows on a hypertable, not in a blob store, so there is no signed-URL upload and no public client key — /api/photos streams the multipart body straight into Postgres. Finished .sog assets ship as static files from Vercel’s CDN and are referenced by rows in the assets table.

Routing: mlx3D fails → Spirula Studio; too few overlapping views → a photo gallery, never called a scan. No measurement → scale_status: unknown, shown as “size not verified” and never placed on a real table at real size.

Asset convention (Y-up, metres): dish origin = plate centre on the table surface · room origin = floor at the entrance · seat view = the seat at eye height ~1.2 m. Every asset stores provenance, backend and captured_on. Debugging: developer mode + USB-C + chrome://inspect, fallback a palm-menu panel writing to debug_logs.

Not used: Google Maps or Places content, scraped review sites, photos of people without consent. Figures above are design budgets from the master plan and vendor documentation, not measured results; the first-hour test measures them.
